name: Cat nip
grown_as: Catnip, a hardy perennial loved by cats, white-flowered and grey-leaved. Garden catmint (Nepeta × faassenii and its kin), much more often grown in borders, is different: lower, with small narrow leaves and lavender-blue flowers. Drawn as true catnip. ⚠️ CHECK which William grows.
habit: An upright, branched, bushy clump 40 to 100 cm high, on square, grey, downy stems.

leaf.arrangement: Opposite, in pairs, each pair at right angles to the one below
leaf.outline: Oval to triangular-oval, 3 to 7 cm long, widest near the base
leaf.margin: Coarse, rather blunt teeth all round from base to tip
leaf.veins: Side veins pressed in, a little wrinkled
leaf.surface: Soft and downy all over, grey-green above, whitish-woolly beneath

flower.petals: Joined; a short, straight upper lip and a larger, spreading lower lip whose broad middle lobe is cupped with a scalloped edge
flower.colour: White, the lower lip dotted with small purple-pink spots
flower.centre: Stamens tucked under the upper lip
flower.behind: A downy, ribbed, tube-shaped green calyx with five pointed teeth
flower.carried: In crowded rings at the top of each stem, making a dense spike-like head 2 to 8 cm long, the lowest rings a little apart

fruit: Four smooth dark brown nutlets in each dry calyx, the heads drying brown. Seeds: small oval dark brown seeds, about 1.5 mm, with a small pale mark at one end.
seedling: Two small rounded seed leaves on stalks; then heart-shaped, toothed, grey-downy true leaves in a pair.
winter: Dies down; a low tuft of small grey leaves often stays at the base.

leaf: an oval leaf with a heart-shaped base and pointed tip
soft grey-green downy surface, paler beneath
bloom: purple-pink spots on the lower lip
crowded into a dense head at the stem top
seedling: first true leaves heart-shaped, toothed and grey
young: a clump of grey-green, heart-shaped, toothed leaves in opposite pairs
flower: dense spiky heads of small white flowers at the stem tops
seedhead: dry brown heads of calyces on the old stems
dormant: a low tuft of small grey leaves at the soil

look_alikes: Garden catmint has small, narrow grey leaves and lavender-blue flowers. Lemon balm is green, not grey, and carries its flowers in the leaf joints. White dead-nettle has bigger white flowers in spaced rings and green leaves. Black horehound has purple flowers and dark green, bad-smelling leaves.
